sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Radnor Township?
sections.html:
Radnor is a Main Line township in Delaware County with high home values, a mandatory township certificate for every resale, and a transfer tax that runs above the county default. A seller who plans around those three items can move quickly, whether the house goes on the market, sells to a neighbor, or goes to a cash buyer.

The township covers about 13.8 square miles and includes Wayne, St. Davids, Rosemont, Ithan, Garrett Hill and Villanova. It is home rule, run by a Board of Commissioners, and it was laid out in 1682 as part of the Welsh Tract. Lancaster Avenue follows the route of the 1794 Philadelphia and Lancaster Turnpike, and the Paoli/Thorndale rail line gave the area its commuter character in the nineteenth century.

Selling fast here mostly comes down to paperwork timing. Buyers, lenders and the township each have steps that can add days, and the sections below set them out in the order you will meet them.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Radnor homes and owners?
sections.html:
Radnor is an expensive, owner-heavy market, and the figures below explain why pricing and buyer financing look different here than in much of Delaware County.

A median value above $800,000 means many sales involve jumbo loans, appraisal scrutiny and long inspection lists. About a third of households rent, so investors and landlords are a real part of the buyer pool near Villanova University and Eastern University.

sections.h2: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell in Radnor?
sections.html:
Yes. The township's FAQ confirms that use and occupancy permits are required for resales, and the Engineering Department issues them. No new owner may occupy the property until the certificate is out.

The Engineering Department's transfer page sets the sequence:

  • The seller files the application at least 10 business days before settlement. The owner signs it, and the fee is $150.
  • Filing 10 days or less before settlement triggers a $300 expedite fee.
  • The township inspects for house number display and public sidewalk condition, then sends a violation notice for anything that needs repair.
  • If sidewalk blocks cannot be replaced before closing, money goes into escrow with the department, and a sidewalk permit is needed for the work.
  • Sellers and buyers both sign a smoke detector and carbon monoxide certification, and the application is not accepted unless the form, the fee and the signed application arrive together.
  • The owner books an inside look at the sanitary sewer soil pipe to confirm there are no illegal connections, and sump pumps must be disconnected from the sanitary system under Chapter 235 of the township code.

Call the Engineering Department at 610-688-5600, extension 129, to book the sewer appointment. Do it the day you file, because that appointment is the step most likely to push a closing date.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax when I sell in Radnor?
sections.html:
Delaware County's Recorder of Deeds lists the state share at 1% and the local share at 1%, with Radnor Township named as an exception at 1.5%. On a sale at the median value above, each additional half percent of local tax is about $4,200, so confirm the exact split with the Recorder before you set a net-proceeds number.

The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue explains that the county Recorder collects the state's 1% along with any local tax. Both the seller (grantor) and the buyer (grantee) are jointly liable, which is why a sales agreement states who pays. Certain transfers between family members, and property passed by will or intestate succession, are exempt under state rules, so an inherited house moving to an heir is treated differently from a market sale.

The county's recording office is at the Government Center in Media, and its transfer tax page lists the state's Statement of Value form (REV-183) for deeds that do not state full consideration. If a deed leaves the price off, that form is what carries the value to the Recorder.

sections.h2: When are Radnor property taxes due, and how do appeals work?
sections.html:
Township bills go out on or before February 1, and the face amount is due May 31. According to the township's FAQ, paying by March 31 earns a 2% discount, and a 10% penalty applies after May 31. The Radnor School District bills and collects its own tax separately, with school bills mailed in July.

An unpaid bill becomes a lien if it is not paid by the end of the calendar year, and the Delaware County Tax Claim Bureau adds interest and penalties. When a house sells, the township asks that you return the bill with the new owner's name, because the Recorder can take more than 60 days to process a title transfer.

  • Assessment appeals go to the Delaware County Board of Assessment Appeals before August 1 for a value effective the following January 1.
  • An appeal does not pause the bill. You pay what is billed and receive a refund or credit if the value drops.
  • The county reassessment that ran from December 2017 to 2020 took effect in January 2021, so current values reflect that base year.
  • A tax certification from the township finance office costs $25 per parcel, and title companies typically request one.

Sewer and stormwater are billed together on a separate mailing around April 1, due May 31. The stormwater charge depends on parcel size, and it applies to all developed properties in the township.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and schools affect a Radnor sale?
sections.html:
Schools drive demand more than any other local factor. Public students attend the Radnor Township School District, which runs Radnor High School, Radnor Middle School, and Radnor, Ithan and Wayne elementary schools. Private options inside the township include Archbishop John Carroll High School, the Agnes Irwin School, the Hill Top Preparatory School and the Valley Forge Military Academy and College.

Buyer groups differ by area. Downtown Wayne has historic districts, with North Wayne and South Wayne as residential pockets around a commercial core. St. Davids and Ithan are quieter residential neighborhoods, while Villanova and Garrett Hill have long-standing Catholic parish communities. Strafford, Bryn Mawr and Villanova straddle township lines, so a listing's mailing address may not match its municipality, and that matters for transfer tax and the certificate.

Commuting helps resale. The township has SEPTA Regional Rail stops at Wayne, St. Davids, Radnor and Villanova, plus seven Norristown High Speed Line stations. U.S. 30 runs along Lancaster Avenue, Route 320 follows Sproul and Spring Mill Roads, and Interstate 476 meets U.S. 30 inside the township.

sections.h2: Which selling route fits a Radnor house?
sections.html:
Three paths cover most sellers, and each handles the township certificate differently.

  • A traditional listing suits houses in good repair. The agent coordinates the certificate, but showings, inspection requests and buyer financing set the schedule.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale saves the commission and leaves you running the certificate, the sewer inspection and the transfer tax paperwork yourself.
  • A cash sale to a company that buys as-is removes lender timing and repairs from the buyer side. The seller still files the township application and still schedules the sewer check, so ask any buyer who does the filing and who pays any sidewalk escrow.

Compare offers on net proceeds, not headline price. Subtract the transfer tax, the $150 or $300 township fee, any sidewalk or sewer repairs, and unpaid taxes before you decide.

faqs.q: Who applies for the certificate of occupancy in Radnor?
faqs.a: The seller does. The application goes to the Radnor Engineering Department at least 10 business days before settlement, signed by the owner, with the $150 fee and the smoke detector and carbon monoxide form signed by seller and buyer.

faqs.q: What happens if my sidewalk is damaged at the time of sale?
faqs.a: The township sends a violation notice after its inspection. If the sidewalk blocks cannot be replaced before settlement, money is placed in escrow with the Engineering Department, and a sidewalk permit is required for the repair.

faqs.q: Is Radnor's transfer tax higher than the rest of Delaware County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's Recorder of Deeds shows most municipalities at the 1% default local share and lists Radnor Township at 1.5%, plus the 1% state tax. Ask the Recorder to confirm the combined figure for your deed.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Radnor house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, but the sewer connection, sidewalk and house number items flagged by the township still have to be corrected or escrowed before the certificate is released. Cosmetic and structural repairs are a matter between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Where do I get a Radnor tax certification for closing?
faqs.a: From the Radnor Township finance office at 301 Iven Avenue in Wayne. The township charges $25 per certification, and you need the parcel (folio) number, the owner name and the address.
